message.content:
The exact count of mitochondria varies widely among different cell types and even within the same cell type under different conditions. In general:

| Cell type (or condition) | Typical mitochondrial count |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Highly active muscle or nerve cells** | ~10 000–30 000 per cell |
| **Typical mammalian somatic cell** | ~500–5 000 per cell |
| **Stem cells or rapidly dividing cells** | ~200–1 000 per cell |
| **Cancer cells with high metabolic rates** | Often >5 000 per cell |

So while there isn’t a single “number” that applies universally, most normal human cells contain somewhere between a few hundred and several thousand mitochondria. The actual number depends on the cell’s energy demands, differentiation state, and environmental cues.
